Subject: DPA language / no-training commitment request

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — product looked solid. Procurement here at DataHealth has a few outstanding items before we can move to signature: primarily we need an explicit contractual commitment that DataHealth interactions won’t be used to improve Redwood models (no-training / no-derivatives), and a current list of subprocessors + their data residency for audit.

Can Redwood provide:
- A short DPA addendum or exhibit that spells out “no training, no derivative model updates” language we can attach to the Master Services Agreement.
- Evidence: an inventory of subprocessors that will touch our data (names, country, role), and confirmation of whether logs/telemetry containing prompts/responses are stored beyond ephemeral caches.
- Any operational artifacts you can share (SOC2 section references, screenshot of subprocessor inventory, or a note on KV/cache retention policy).

We have a compliance window and would like to target signature by EOD Apr 6 if possible. Please let me know the quickest way to get this into our contracts team — we prefer a DocuSign-ready package and a one-pager describing the operational controls.

Thanks,
Marcus Lee
Director, Procurement
DataHealth

Lauren / Marissa — rough draft language below that I think balances the ask with operational constraints. Putting it here so we can iterate quickly: feel free to paste into a DPA exhibit.

Proposed exhibit language (draft):
"Customer Data Use; No Training
1. Redwood Inference agrees that Customer Content (prompts, responses, attachments, and other data submitted by Customer or its end users during the provision of Services) will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's models or model parameters. Redwood will not derive or transfer Customer Content to third parties for the purpose of model training.
2. Redwood may process aggregated, de-identified telemetry for system performance, monitoring, and capacity planning, provided such telemetry cannot reasonably be re-associated with Customer Content or individual end users.
3. Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide an attestation of compliance and a snapshot of the subprocessor inventory applicable to Customer's Services, including subprocessors' country of operation and role.
4. This exhibit supersedes any contrary language in the Master DPA solely to the extent necessary to enforce the no-training commitment described herein.

Operational notes for Marissa: we should attach a CSV listing each subprocessor, their primary function, country, and whether they have access to content-level data or solely to telemetry/metrics. For retention/ops proof, provide the KV cache retention policy (e.g., ephemeral cache TTL: 5 minutes; logs kept for operational troubleshooting: 7 days; exports require internal approval).

If that's acceptable, Lauren — I can produce the docx addendum and a one‑pager attestation. Marissa — can you generate the subprocessor CSV and a short ops note by EOD tomorrow?

Ben Carter
Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
